**1. Executive Summary**

This report presents the findings of the annual energy audit conducted at GreenOrchid Tech Park for the calendar year 2023. The primary objective was to verify the total energy consumption, analyse the consumption pattern across different building systems and blocks, and identify cost-effective measures for reducing energy use without compromising occupant comfort.

The total energy consumption for the site during 2023 was recorded and verified through a combination of main meter readings, sub-meter data, and billing records from Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited (BESCOM). According to the Energy Audit Report by Vantaa Energy Solutions, GreenOrchid Tech Park's annual_energy_consumption_2023 was recorded as 4850000 kWh. Record status: current. This figure is considered current and forms the baseline for all future energy performance comparisons and savings calculations presented in this document.

Compared to the previous audit period (2022), the total consumption shows an increase of approximately 4.3%, which correlates with the addition of the new Wing C office floors (floors 7 and 8) that were occupied in May 2023. However, the Energy Performance Index (EPI) per square meter has improved slightly due to the increased occupied area.

We have identified a combined energy saving potential of approximately 485,000 kWh per annum (about 10% of current consumption) through a series of measures including HVAC scheduling optimisation, LED retrofits in common areas, and power factor correction. The detailed recommendations are provided in Section 7.

---

**2. Methodology**

The audit was carried out following the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) guidelines for commercial buildings. The methodology involved the following steps:

1.  **Data Collection:** Collection of BESCOM electricity bills for all 12 months of 2023, main meter readings (daily, where available), and sub-meter readings for individual blocks, HVAC systems, lifts, and external lighting.
2.  **Site Walk-through:** Physical inspection of all electrical rooms, the central chiller plant, AHU rooms, lift machine rooms, and external lighting panels. We recorded connected load details and operational schedules.
3.  **Measurement:** Spot measurements of power quality parameters (voltage, current, power factor, THD) using a Fluke 435 Series II power quality analyser at the main LT panel and key sub-distribution boards.
4.  **Data Analysis:** Normalisation of consumption data for weather variations (degree-days) and occupancy. Benchmarking of EPI against similar IT parks in the region.
5.  **Stakeholder Interviews:** Discussions with the site facility manager, Mr. Rajesh Menon, and the shift-in-charge electrical engineers regarding operating practices and known issues.

**Limitations:** Sub-metering for the data centre (Block B, Basement) was found to be non-functional for the months of April and May 2023. Consumption for these two months was estimated based on the average of March and June 2023 readings for that sub-meter. This estimation is noted in the detailed tables where applicable.

**4. Energy Efficiency Measures Implemented in 2024**

During 2024, the facility management team, with technical support from Vantaa Energy Solutions, implemented a set of measures recommended in the preliminary audit findings. The major measures are described below.

**4.1 HVAC Optimisation (Chilled Water System)**

The central chiller plant consists of three 350 TR water-cooled chillers. The following changes were made:

- Chiller sequencing logic revised to match part-load conditions; the previous schedule often ran two chillers at low load instead of one at near-full load.
- Chilled water supply temperature set point increased from 6.5°C to 7.5°C during non-peak hours (22:00–06:00).
- Condenser water pump speed control enabled via VFD; previously pumps ran at fixed speed throughout the year.
- AHU supply fan VFDs were already installed; the minimum speed limit was reduced from 45% to 35% during unoccupied periods.

Estimated annual savings from HVAC measures: 3,85,000 kWh.

**4.2 LED Retrofits in Common Areas**

The Energy Audit Report by Vantaa Energy Solutions shows GreenOrchid Tech Park energy_savings_percentage_2024 as 12.5 percent. Record status: current.

All 1,240 CFL and 380 halogen fixtures in corridors, stairwells, parking basement, and external walkways were replaced with LED equivalents (18W and 9W respectively). This work was completed in February 2024. Light levels were verified to meet the recommended lux levels for each area after replacement.

Estimated annual savings: 1,05,000 kWh.

**4.3 Power Factor Correction**

The existing capacitor bank (2 × 150 kVAR) was found to be operating with one bank out of service. After repair and addition of a third 150 kVAR bank, the average power factor improved from 0.87 to 0.96. This reduced distribution losses and the kVA demand charges.

Estimated annual savings: 42,000 kWh (including reduced I²R losses in feeders).

**4.4 Other Minor Measures**

- Timer-based control for external decorative lighting (reduced from 12 hours to 6 hours per night).
- Removal of 12 old CRT monitors from the security control room, replaced with LED monitors.
- Air curtain units at the main entrance lobby set to operate only when the main doors are open, using a door contact sensor.

Combined estimated savings from minor measures: 18,000 kWh.
## 5. Seasonal Energy Consumption Analysis

### 5.2 Seasonal Observations

**Summer (April–June):** Consumption peaked in May at 8,91,200 kWh, driven by continuous chiller operation and high ambient temperatures. The peak demand of 1,210 kVA occurred during the second week of May when all three chiller plants were online simultaneously. This period also recorded the lowest average power factor (0.87), primarily due to the capacitor bank issue identified during the audit.

**Monsoon (July–September):** A gradual decline in consumption was observed, consistent with reduced ambient temperatures. However, humidity levels necessitated continued dehumidification, limiting the reduction in HVAC load. The SEB billing for August showed a 2.1% higher consumption than our meter readings; this was traced to a CT ratio mismatch in the billing meter, which the SEB corrected in the September bill.

**Post-monsoon and Winter (October–January):** The most significant reduction occurred during this period. The Diwali shutdown in October accounted for approximately 18,000 kWh of savings compared to a normal working month. December and January recorded the lowest monthly consumption figures, as the chillers operated at minimum load and were frequently cycled off during weekends. Occupancy during this period was lower due to year-end holidays and the Pongal break in January.

**Early Spring (February–March):** The combined effect of the LED retrofit, PF correction, and revised chiller sequencing became fully apparent in these months. February consumption of 6,58,900 kWh was 26.1% lower than the same month in the previous year (8,91,400 kWh in Feb 2023). The average power factor improved to 0.94 in February and 0.96 in March, confirming the effectiveness of the capacitor bank repairs.

### 5.3 Occupancy Impact Analysis

Occupancy data was obtained from the access control system and verified against the tenant-wise floor usage reports submitted by the facility management team. The correlation between occupancy and energy consumption was strongest for lighting and plug loads, which together account for approximately 38% of total consumption.
# 6. RECOMMENDED MEASURES AND IMPLEMENTATION PLAN

The following recommendations are presented in order of priority, based on the findings detailed in Sections 4 and 5 of this report. Each measure includes the estimated capital cost, expected annual savings, simple payback period, and a proposed implementation timeline. These recommendations supersede the preliminary list circulated in the interim report dated 15 January 2024; two measures from that list (installation of variable frequency drives on the cooling tower fans and replacement of the existing DG set with a higher-efficiency model) have been deferred pending further feasibility analysis and are not included below.

All costs are in INR and include material, installation, commissioning, and applicable taxes. Savings estimates are based on the consumption baseline established in Section 5.1 and assume the current tariff structure remains unchanged. Where savings depend on operational changes, the relevant assumptions are noted.

## 6.1 Priority Measures

### 6.1.1 LED Retrofit – Phase II (Car Park and Common Areas)

The Phase I LED retrofit, completed in November 2023, covered the office floors and produced the savings discussed in Section 5.2. Phase II extends the same programme to the basement car park, stairwells, and external perimeter lighting.

- **Scope:** Replacement of 420 existing fluorescent and CFL fittings with LED luminaires; installation of occupancy sensors in stairwells and car park zones with low footfall.
- **Estimated Cost:** INR 14,80,000
- **Expected Annual Savings:** 1,12,500 kWh (approximately INR 9,55,000 at the current blended tariff of INR 8.49/kWh)
- **Simple Payback:** 1.6 years
- **Implementation Timeline:** April–May 2024. Procurement to be initiated immediately after approval. Installation to be scheduled outside business hours to minimise disruption.

### 6.1.2 Chiller Sequencing Optimisation – Software Upgrade

The revised chiller sequencing protocol described in Section 5.2 was implemented manually by the operations team in January 2024. This measure formalises the protocol through a software upgrade to the building management system (BMS), enabling automatic sequencing based on real-time load and ambient conditions.

- **Scope:** Upgrade of BMS software (Siemens Desigo CC, current version 5.1) to enable predictive chiller staging; configuration of load-shedding logic for peak demand periods; operator training.
- **Estimated Cost:** INR 6,20,000
- **Expected Annual Savings:** 1,85,000 kWh (approximately INR 15,70,000). This estimate is conservative and based on the savings observed during the manual implementation period (February–March 2024), annualised with a 15% discount to account for seasonal variation.
- **Simple Payback:** 0.4 years
- **Implementation Timeline:** June–July 2024. BMS vendor to be mobilised in the first week of June. System downtime during the upgrade will be limited to one weekend.

### 6.1.3 Power Factor Correction – Capacitor Bank Replacement

The existing capacitor bank, rated at 300 kVAr, was found to have two failed capacitor units and one defective contactor during the audit (see Section 4.3). Temporary repairs were carried out in January 2024, restoring the average power factor to 0.94. This measure provides a permanent solution.

### 6.1.4 AHU Fan Motor Replacement

The audit identified six air handling units (AHUs) on the 3rd and 4th floors operating with oversized motors (11 kW rated, average operating load 6.2 kW). These motors operate at low efficiency due to part-load operation.

- **Scope:** Replacement of six 11 kW motors with 7.5 kW high-efficiency (IE3) motors; installation of variable frequency drives (VFDs) on the supply fans; re-balancing of duct static pressure.
- **Estimated Cost:** INR 8,75,000 (including VFDs and commissioning)
- **Expected Annual Savings:** 68,400 kWh (approximately INR 5,81,000)
- **Simple Payback:** 1.5 years
- **Implementation Timeline:** August–September 2024. Work to be carried out floor-by-floor to maintain partial occupancy comfort. Each AHU will be out of service for a maximum of two days.

**1. Executive Summary**

This report presents the findings of the annual energy audit conducted at GreenOrchid Tech Park for the calendar year 2023. The primary objective was to verify the total energy consumption, analyse the consumption pattern across different building systems and blocks, and identify cost-effective measures for reducing energy use without compromising occupant comfort.

The total energy consumption for the site during 2023 was recorded and verified through a combination of main meter readings, sub-meter data, and billing records from Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited (BESCOM). According to the Energy Audit Report by Vantaa Energy Solutions, GreenOrchid Tech Park's annual_energy_consumption_2023 was recorded as 4850000 kWh. Record status: current. This figure is considered current and forms the baseline for all future energy performance comparisons and savings calculations presented in this document.

Compared to the previous audit period (2022), the total consumption shows an increase of approximately 4.3%, which correlates with the addition of the new Wing C office floors (floors 7 and 8) that were occupied in May 2023. However, the Energy Performance Index (EPI) per square meter has improved slightly due to the increased occupied area.

We have identified a combined energy saving potential of approximately 485,000 kWh per annum (about 10% of current consumption) through a series of measures including HVAC scheduling optimisation, LED retrofits in common areas, and power factor correction. The detailed recommendations are provided in Section 7.

---

**2. Methodology**

The audit was carried out following the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) guidelines for commercial buildings. The methodology involved the following steps:

1.  **Data Collection:** Collection of BESCOM electricity bills for all 12 months of 2023, main meter readings (daily, where available), and sub-meter readings for individual blocks, HVAC systems, lifts, and external lighting.
2.  **Site Walk-through:** Physical inspection of all electrical rooms, the central chiller plant, AHU rooms, lift machine rooms, and external lighting panels. We recorded connected load details and operational schedules.
3.  **Measurement:** Spot measurements of power quality parameters (voltage, current, power factor, THD) using a Fluke 435 Series II power quality analyser at the main LT panel and key sub-distribution boards.
4.  **Data Analysis:** Normalisation of consumption data for weather variations (degree-days) and occupancy. Benchmarking of EPI against similar IT parks in the region.
5.  **Stakeholder Interviews:** Discussions with the site facility manager, Mr. Rajesh Menon, and the shift-in-charge electrical engineers regarding operating practices and known issues.

**Limitations:** Sub-metering for the data centre (Block B, Basement) was found to be non-functional for the months of April and May 2023. Consumption for these two months was estimated based on the average of March and June 2023 readings for that sub-meter. This estimation is noted in the detailed tables where applicable.

**4. Energy Efficiency Measures Implemented in 2024**

During 2024, the facility management team, with technical support from Vantaa Energy Solutions, implemented a set of measures recommended in the preliminary audit findings. The major measures are described below.

**4.1 HVAC Optimisation (Chilled Water System)**

The central chiller plant consists of three 350 TR water-cooled chillers. The following changes were made:

- Chiller sequencing logic revised to match part-load conditions; the previous schedule often ran two chillers at low load instead of one at near-full load.
- Chilled water supply temperature set point increased from 6.5°C to 7.5°C during non-peak hours (22:00–06:00).
- Condenser water pump speed control enabled via VFD; previously pumps ran at fixed speed throughout the year.
- AHU supply fan VFDs were already installed; the minimum speed limit was reduced from 45% to 35% during unoccupied periods.

**4.2 LED Retrofits in Common Areas**

The Energy Audit Report by Vantaa Energy Solutions shows GreenOrchid Tech Park energy_savings_percentage_2024 as 12.5 percent. Record status: current.

All 1,240 CFL and 380 halogen fixtures in corridors, stairwells, parking basement, and external walkways were replaced with LED equivalents (18W and 9W respectively). This work was completed in February 2024. Light levels were verified to meet the recommended lux levels for each area after replacement.

Estimated annual savings: 1,05,000 kWh.

**4.3 Power Factor Correction**

The existing capacitor bank (2 × 150 kVAR) was found to be operating with one bank out of service. After repair and addition of a third 150 kVAR bank, the average power factor improved from 0.87 to 0.96. This reduced distribution losses and the kVA demand charges.

Estimated annual savings: 42,000 kWh (including reduced I²R losses in feeders).

**4.4 Other Minor Measures**

- Timer-based control for external decorative lighting (reduced from 12 hours to 6 hours per night).
- Removal of 12 old CRT monitors from the security control room, replaced with LED monitors.
- Air curtain units at the main entrance lobby set to operate only when the main doors are open, using a door contact sensor.

### 5.2 Seasonal Observations

**Summer (April–June):** Consumption peaked in May at 8,91,200 kWh, driven by continuous chiller operation and high ambient temperatures. The peak demand of 1,210 kVA occurred during the second week of May when all three chiller plants were online simultaneously. This period also recorded the lowest average power factor (0.87), primarily due to the capacitor bank issue identified during the audit.

**Monsoon (July–September):** A gradual decline in consumption was observed, consistent with reduced ambient temperatures. However, humidity levels necessitated continued dehumidification, limiting the reduction in HVAC load. The SEB billing for August showed a 2.1% higher consumption than our meter readings; this was traced to a CT ratio mismatch in the billing meter, which the SEB corrected in the September bill.

**Post-monsoon and Winter (October–January):** The most significant reduction occurred during this period. The Diwali shutdown in October accounted for approximately 18,000 kWh of savings compared to a normal working month. December and January recorded the lowest monthly consumption figures, as the chillers operated at minimum load and were frequently cycled off during weekends. Occupancy during this period was lower due to year-end holidays and the Pongal break in January.

**Early Spring (February–March):** The combined effect of the LED retrofit, PF correction, and revised chiller sequencing became fully apparent in these months. February consumption of 6,58,900 kWh was 26.1% lower than the same month in the previous year (8,91,400 kWh in Feb 2023). The average power factor improved to 0.94 in February and 0.96 in March, confirming the effectiveness of the capacitor bank repairs.

### 5.3 Occupancy Impact Analysis

Occupancy data was obtained from the access control system and verified against the tenant-wise floor usage reports submitted by the facility management team. The correlation between occupancy and energy consumption was strongest for lighting and plug loads, which together account for approximately 38% of total consumption.

# 6. RECOMMENDED MEASURES AND IMPLEMENTATION PLAN

The following recommendations are presented in order of priority, based on the findings detailed in Sections 4 and 5 of this report. Each measure includes the estimated capital cost, expected annual savings, simple payback period, and a proposed implementation timeline. These recommendations supersede the preliminary list circulated in the interim report dated 15 January 2024; two measures from that list (installation of variable frequency drives on the cooling tower fans and replacement of the existing DG set with a higher-efficiency model) have been deferred pending further feasibility analysis and are not included below.

All costs are in INR and include material, installation, commissioning, and applicable taxes. Savings estimates are based on the consumption baseline established in Section 5.1 and assume the current tariff structure remains unchanged. Where savings depend on operational changes, the relevant assumptions are noted.

## 6.1 Priority Measures

### 6.1.1 LED Retrofit – Phase II (Car Park and Common Areas)

The Phase I LED retrofit, completed in November 2023, covered the office floors and produced the savings discussed in Section 5.2. Phase II extends the same programme to the basement car park, stairwells, and external perimeter lighting.

- **Scope:** Replacement of 420 existing fluorescent and CFL fittings with LED luminaires; installation of occupancy sensors in stairwells and car park zones with low footfall.
- **Estimated Cost:** INR 14,80,000
- **Expected Annual Savings:** 1,12,500 kWh (approximately INR 9,55,000 at the current blended tariff of INR 8.49/kWh)
- **Simple Payback:** 1.6 years
- **Implementation Timeline:** April–May 2024. Procurement to be initiated immediately after approval. Installation to be scheduled outside business hours to minimise disruption.

### 6.1.2 Chiller Sequencing Optimisation – Software Upgrade

The revised chiller sequencing protocol described in Section 5.2 was implemented manually by the operations team in January 2024. This measure formalises the protocol through a software upgrade to the building management system (BMS), enabling automatic sequencing based on real-time load and ambient conditions.

- **Scope:** Upgrade of BMS software (Siemens Desigo CC, current version 5.1) to enable predictive chiller staging; configuration of load-shedding logic for peak demand periods; operator training.
- **Estimated Cost:** INR 6,20,000
- **Expected Annual Savings:** 1,85,000 kWh (approximately INR 15,70,000). This estimate is conservative and based on the savings observed during the manual implementation period (February–March 2024), annualised with a 15% discount to account for seasonal variation.
- **Simple Payback:** 0.4 years
- **Implementation Timeline:** June–July 2024. BMS vendor to be mobilised in the first week of June. System downtime during the upgrade will be limited to one weekend.

### 6.1.3 Power Factor Correction – Capacitor Bank Replacement

The existing capacitor bank, rated at 300 kVAr, was found to have two failed capacitor units and one defective contactor during the audit (see Section 4.3). Temporary repairs were carried out in January 2024, restoring the average power factor to 0.94. This measure provides a permanent solution.

### 6.1.4 AHU Fan Motor Replacement

The audit identified six air handling units (AHUs) on the 3rd and 4th floors operating with oversized motors (11 kW rated, average operating load 6.2 kW). These motors operate at low efficiency due to part-load operation.

- **Scope:** Replacement of six 11 kW motors with 7.5 kW high-efficiency (IE3) motors; installation of variable frequency drives (VFDs) on the supply fans; re-balancing of duct static pressure.
- **Estimated Cost:** INR 8,75,000 (including VFDs and commissioning)
- **Expected Annual Savings:** 68,400 kWh (approximately INR 5,81,000)
- **Simple Payback:** 1.5 years
- **Implementation Timeline:** August–September 2024. Work to be carried out floor-by-floor to maintain partial occupancy comfort. Each AHU will be out of service for a maximum of two days.
